hypothesis_or_artifact: The independence assumption under every exact binomial and exact sign test in the register - H2's two-look boundary (Amendments H2-3 Change 3, H2-4 section 3) and H1's P3, the register's only PASS
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: The look-2 spend is computed conditional on not having rejected at look 1, over the independent increment Bin(n2 - n1, 1/2), so the total type-I error is at most alpha1 + alpha2 = 0.05 exactly, with no asymptotic approximation anywhere.
evidence_summary: Every verdict statistic here is an exact binomial or exact sign test over per-event or per-pair indicators, whose exact tails require independent Bernoulli trials. The registration never states, justifies or tests that assumption: a grep for independen|cluster|overlapping|design effect across the snapshot returns only prior-slot labels, H5's 'independent underlying feed', and 'the independent increment' in the challenged quote. The design guarantees dependence by construction - 'With replacement: one old perp may serve as control for many events' (REGISTRATION.md:176, carried into H2 at registrations/H2/REGISTRATION.md:129-130) and all pairs are 30-day windows on one venue with entries spanning 2026-05-30 to 2026-08-28 (report.md:516). Measured from the live ledgers: H1 pairs.jsonl 176 rows over 82 distinct controls, top control serves 15 pairs, top five serve 47 of 176, effective distinct-control count 1/sum(p^2) about 41, mean pair overlapping 12.6 others within +/-30 days; H2 h2_pairs.jsonl 63 rows over 34 distinct controls with 28 mutually overlapping windows. The register corrects for multiplicity in four separate places (REGISTRATION.md:200-201; registrations/H2/REGISTRATION.md:182-189, :500-501; registrations/H4/REGISTRATION.md:79-81) and nowhere for dependence. Sensitivity: an intra-cluster correlation of 1-2 percent consumes or exceeds the whole familywise budget at look 1 and flips P3. Stated honestly against the thesis: breaking P3 needs a design effect of about 4x (175 -> ~41 effective), which is the same order as the measured effective control count but is not established, and no rho has been measured because the outcome values are sealed and barred to this audit.
recomputation: Inputs: n1=59, k1=38, n2=117, k2=69 from ktable_amended.json boundaries.at_look2_min_n (alpha_spent_look1 0.018172, alpha_spent_look2 0.024025); P3 = 114 of 175 from reports/stage_b/read.json (statistic 3.766632285793312e-05); control-reuse and window-overlap structure from the live ledgers. Method: replace the i.i.d. null Bin(n, 1/2) with a beta-binomial null of the same mean and intra-cluster correlation rho (rho=0 reproduces every registered figure exactly), scipy.stats.betabinom.sf. Results: P(S1>=38 | n1=59) rho=0 -> 0.0182 (registered spend), rho=0.01 -> 0.0486, rho=0.02 -> 0.0791. P(S>=69 | n=117) rho=0 -> 0.0320, rho=0.01 -> 0.1050, rho=0.02 -> 0.1575. P3 at 114/175: rho=0 -> 3.767e-05 (reproduces the registered figure), rho=0.01 -> 8.35e-03, rho=0.02 -> 3.13e-02 i.e. FAIL against alpha_adj=0.016952. By effective n at share 0.6514: PASS holds at n_eff >= 50 (p=1.64e-02), fails from n_eff about 41. Measured effective distinct-control count 1/sum(p^2) about 41 over 176 pairs.
would_resolve: Either a registered dependence model (a cluster-robust or permutation/bootstrap null over control clusters and calendar blocks, with the boundaries recomputed under it); or a stated and defended independence assumption plus a measurement of the design effect from quantities already on disk (control reuse and entry-date overlap are computable without opening any outcome); or an explicit epistemic-boundary sentence that the exact tails are conditional on an independence the design does not provide.
confidence: HIGH on the assumption being unstated and structurally violated; MEDIUM that a registered verdict changes
confidence_why: The reuse rule is registered and the window overlap is measured from the repository's own ledgers, so the violation is certain; but the design effect required to flip P3 is about 4x and no rho has been measured, so no verdict is demonstrated wrong.
invalidation_note: The only post-anchor commit (dff1663, 2026-09-10, Amendment H5-3) touches H5's fire-date projection; H2's boundary and H1's spent read are unchanged. A future amendment registering a dependence model would resolve this rather than invalidate it.

claim_quote: Registered power assumption: true share 0.65 - generating-sample-derived (P3 pair share 114/175 = 0.651).
evidence_summary: P3's success event, read from the code that produced 114/175, is 'successes = sum(1 for _, net, control in pairs if net > control)' with both terms net_short_30 (src/npl/verdict.py:136), where net_short = price + funding - cost per instrument class (src/npl/outcome.py:24-27) and a control's class comes from its own dex (REGISTRATION.md:519-522), so P3's indicator is G - c_young + c_elder > 0. The two thresholds differ by exactly 2 x the elder leg's round-trip cost - 18 bp where the elder is main-dex vanilla (9 bp central) and 36 bp where it is HIP-3 (18 bp central), per REGISTRATION.md:148-151 and src/npl/config.py:180-181. Difference in threshold = 2*c_e in {18 bp, 36 bp}. The magnitude of the share difference cannot be computed without the sealed distribution; the sign is certain. For scale, the registered mean paired price differential is +6.43 points over n = 175 (REGISTRATION.md:578-580; reports/stage_b/read.json secondaries/h8_paired_30d mean_price_term_diff 0.06426309349214424).

confidence: HIGH on direction; LOW on magnitude
confidence_why: It is algebra over two code paths in the snapshot, so the direction is certain; the magnitude of the share shift cannot be computed without the sealed outcome distribution.
